mission_phase: Generation 17 - Shopify Hardening via Real-Store Shakedown
focus: Before any non-Shopify expansion, prove the platform does a good job on Shopify: run the complete cycle (onboard, inspect, curate, re-inspect, executive report/PDF, fix plan) across real Shopify retailers in different verticals and honestly collect what works and what breaks.
reason_generation_started: Ferosh directed consolidation on Shopify quality before going further. This also satisfies the standing planning gate: architecture expands only after real inspections produce observed capability gaps.
primary_deliverable: A shakedown record across five verticals (footwear, home goods, athletic apparel, socks/basics, beauty) with per-store cycle outcomes, observed capability gaps, curation quality notes, and a hardening backlog derived from evidence rather than speculation.
validation_notes: VAL-064 records the five-store shakedown and the first hardening fix.
Pipeline robustness confirmed across five verticals; no crashes, honest degradation throughout.
Platform detected Shopify High on Allbirds, Brooklinen, Gymshark, ColourPop; Bombas fell to unknown (public JSON endpoints 404).
Dominant finding FND-GEN017-001 (operational-collection leakage in curation) fixed and proven by re-curation from retained evidence.

VAL-066 (consolidation) is the second independent clean pass: curation hardening re-verified deterministic (no promo/ops leak), Dress Up GEN-012 parity held, all suites clean with no implementation changes since the last commit.
known_gaps_opened: FND-GEN017-002: Shopify stores that disable public JSON endpoints (Bombas) are not detected or curated; adapter needs a fallback or the report needs clearer framing.
FND-GEN017-003: curated queries can lower coverage vs the starter run with no guard.
FND-GEN017-004: report issue emission does not weight query confidence (mitigated by the curation fix).
FND-GEN017-005: DS3 attribute lexicon is apparel-biased; home-goods/beauty yield no attribute rows.
